passages.text: But God remembered Noah and all the animals and livestock that were with him in the ark. And God sent a wind over the earth, and the waters began to subside.
passages.sermon:
God remembered Noah.
God remembered all the animals with Noah in the ark.
God remembered all the livestock with Noah in the ark.
God sent a wind over the earth.
The waters began to go down.
passages.original: וַיִּזְכֹּ֤ר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־ נֹ֔חַ וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־ הַֽחַיָּה֙ וְאֶת־ כָּל־ הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בַּתֵּבָ֑ה וַיַּעֲבֵ֨ר אֱלֹהִ֥ים ר֙וּחַ֙ עַל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ וַיָּשֹׁ֖כּוּ הַמָּֽיִם׃

passages.text: The springs of the deep and the floodgates of the heavens were closed, and the rain from the sky was restrained.
passages.sermon:
God acted to stop the flood.
God closed the springs under the earth.
God shut the floodgates in the sky.
God stopped the rain from falling from the sky.
passages.original: וַיִּסָּֽכְרוּ֙ מַעְיְנֹ֣ת תְּה֔וֹם וַֽאֲרֻבֹּ֖ת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַיִּכָּלֵ֥א הַגֶּ֖שֶׁם מִן־ הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

passages.text: The waters receded steadily from the earth, and after 150 days the waters had gone down.
passages.sermon:
God sent a flood over the earth.
The waters covered the land.
The waters began to recede from the earth.
The waters kept going down, little by little.
This continued for a long time.
After 150 days, the waters had gone down.
passages.original: וַיָּשֻׁ֧בוּ הַמַּ֛יִם מֵעַ֥ל הָאָ֖רֶץ הָל֣וֹךְ וָשׁ֑וֹב וַיַּחְסְר֣וּ הַמַּ֔יִם מִקְצֵ֕ה חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּמְאַ֖ת יֽוֹם׃

passages.text: On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
passages.sermon:
Noah built an ark.
God sent a flood over the earth.
The flood covered the land for many days.
The waters began to go down.
On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark stopped moving.
The ark rested on the mountains of Ararat.
passages.original: וַתָּ֤נַח הַתֵּבָה֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָה־ עָשָׂ֥ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ עַ֖ל הָרֵ֥י אֲרָרָֽט׃

passages.text: And the waters continued to recede until the tenth month, and on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains became visible.
passages.sermon:
God sent a great flood over the earth.
The waters covered everything.
The waters kept going down.
This continued until the tenth month.
On the first day of the tenth month, something changed.
People could see the tops of the mountains.
passages.original: וְהַמַּ֗יִם הָיוּ֙ הָל֣וֹךְ וְחָס֔וֹר עַ֖ד הַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽעֲשִׂירִ֑י בָּֽעֲשִׂירִי֙ בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ נִרְא֖וּ רָאשֵׁ֥י הֶֽהָרִֽים׃

passages.text: After forty days Noah opened the window he had made in the ark and sent out a raven. It kept flying back and forth until the waters had dried up from the earth.
passages.sermon:
Noah was a righteous man.
God saved Noah and his family from the flood.
Noah built an ark as God commanded.
Noah and his family stayed in the ark during the flood.
After forty days, Noah opened the window he had made in the ark.
Noah sent out a raven from the ark.
The raven went out.
The raven kept flying back and forth.
The raven did this until the waters dried up from the earth.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֑וֹם וַיִּפְתַּ֣ח נֹ֔חַ אֶת־ חַלּ֥וֹן הַתֵּבָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃ וַיְשַׁלַּ֖ח אֶת־ הָֽעֹרֵ֑ב וַיֵּצֵ֤א יָצוֹא֙ וָשׁ֔וֹב עַד־ יְבֹ֥שֶׁת הַמַּ֖יִם מֵעַ֥ל הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Then Noah sent out a dove to see if the waters had receded from the surface of the ground.
passages.sermon:
Noah was inside the ark.
Noah wanted to know if the floodwaters had gone down.
Noah took a dove.
Noah sent the dove out from the ark.
Noah wanted to see if the waters had receded from the surface of the ground.
passages.original: וַיְשַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־ הַיּוֹנָ֖ה מֵאִתּ֑וֹ לִרְאוֹת֙ הֲקַ֣לּוּ הַמַּ֔יִם מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֥י הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃

passages.text: But the dove found no place to rest her foot, and she returned to him in the ark, because the waters were still covering the surface of all the earth. So he reached out his hand and brought her back inside the ark.
passages.sermon:
Noah was inside the ark.
He sent out a dove.
The dove looked for a place to rest her foot.
She found no place to rest.
The waters still covered the surface of all the earth.
The dove returned to Noah in the ark.
Noah reached out his hand.
He took the dove.
He brought her back inside the ark.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ מָצְאָה֩ הַיּוֹנָ֨ה מָנ֜וֹחַ לְכַף־ רַגְלָ֗הּ וַתָּ֤שָׁב אֵלָיו֙ אֶל־ הַתֵּבָ֔ה כִּי־ מַ֖יִם עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י כָל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָדוֹ֙ וַיִּקָּחֶ֔הָ וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתָ֛הּ אֵלָ֖יו אֶל־ הַתֵּבָֽה׃

passages.text: Noah waited seven more days and again sent out the dove from the ark.
passages.sermon: Noah was inside the ark.\r\nNoah waited seven more days.\r\nNoah sent out the dove again from the ark.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣חֶל ע֔וֹד שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וַיֹּ֛סֶף שַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־ הַיּוֹנָ֖ה מִן־ הַתֵּבָֽה׃

passages.text: And behold, the dove returned to him in the evening with a freshly plucked olive leaf in her beak. So Noah knew that the waters had receded from the earth.
passages.sermon:
Noah was inside the ark.
Noah had sent out a dove from the ark.
The dove returned to Noah in the evening.
The dove had a freshly picked olive leaf in her beak.
Noah saw the olive leaf.
Noah understood that the waters had gone down from the earth.
passages.original: וַתָּבֹ֨א אֵלָ֤יו הַיּוֹנָה֙ לְעֵ֣ת עֶ֔רֶב וְהִנֵּ֥ה עֲלֵה־ זַ֖יִת טָרָ֣ף בְּפִ֑יהָ וַיֵּ֣דַע נֹ֔חַ כִּי־ קַ֥לּוּ הַמַּ֖יִם מֵעַ֥ל הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: And Noah waited seven more days and sent out the dove again, but this time she did not return to him.
passages.sermon:
Noah was a righteous man.
Noah was inside the ark.
Noah waited seven more days.
Noah sent out the dove again from the ark.
The dove did not return to Noah.
passages.original: וַיִּיָּ֣חֶל ע֔וֹד שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וַיְשַׁלַּח֙ אֶת־ הַיּוֹנָ֔ה וְלֹֽא־ יָסְפָ֥ה שׁוּב־ אֵלָ֖יו עֽוֹד׃

passages.text: In Noah’s six hundred and first year, on the first day of the first month, the waters had dried up from the earth. So Noah removed the covering from the ark and saw that the surface of the ground was dry.
passages.sermon:
Noah was six hundred and one years old.
It was the first day of the first month.
The waters had dried up from the earth.
Noah removed the covering from the ark.
Noah looked out.
He saw that the surface of the ground was dry.
passages.original: וַֽ֠יְהִי בְּאַחַ֨ת וְשֵׁשׁ־ מֵא֜וֹת שָׁנָ֗ה בָּֽרִאשׁוֹן֙ בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ חָֽרְב֥וּ הַמַּ֖יִם מֵעַ֣ל הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיָּ֤סַר נֹ֙חַ֙ אֶת־ מִכְסֵ֣ה הַתֵּבָ֔ה וַיַּ֕רְא וְהִנֵּ֥ה חָֽרְב֖וּ פְּנֵ֥י הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃

passages.text: By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was fully dry.
passages.sermon: The earth became fully dry.\r\nThis happened on the twenty-seventh day of the second month.
passages.original: וּבַחֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָ֧ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֛ים י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ יָבְשָׁ֖ה הָאָֽרֶץ׃ס

passages.text: Then God said to Noah, “Come out of the ark, you and your wife, along with your sons and their wives.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Noah.
God said, “Come out of the ark.
Bring your wife with you.
Bring your sons with you.
Bring your sons’ wives with you.
All of you come out together.”
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־ נֹ֥חַ לֵאמֹֽר׃ צֵ֖א מִן־ הַתֵּבָ֑ה אַתָּ֕ה וְאִשְׁתְּךָ֛ וּבָנֶ֥יךָ וּנְשֵֽׁי־ בָנֶ֖יךָ אִתָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: Bring out all the living creatures that are with you—birds, livestock, and everything that crawls upon the ground—so that they can spread out over the earth and be fruitful and multiply upon it.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Noah.
God told Noah to bring out all the living creatures with him.
These creatures included every kind of animal.
They included every kind of bird.
They included every kind of livestock.
They included every creature that crawls on the ground.
God told Noah to bring them all out of the ark.
God wanted these creatures to fill the earth.
God wanted them to have many offspring.
God wanted them to become many on the earth.
passages.original: כָּל־ הַחַיָּ֨ה אֲשֶֽׁר־ אִתְּךָ֜ מִכָּל־ בָּשָׂ֗ר בָּע֧וֹף וּבַבְּהֵמָ֛ה וּבְכָל־ הָרֶ֛מֶשׂ הָרֹמֵ֥שׂ עַל־ הָאָ֖רֶץ הוֹצֵא אִתָּ֑ךְ וְשָֽׁרְצ֣וּ בָאָ֔רֶץ וּפָר֥וּ וְרָב֖וּ עַל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: So Noah came out, along with his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives.
passages.sermon:
Noah was a righteous man.
Noah survived the flood in the ark.
Noah came out of the ark.
Noah’s sons came out with him.
Noah’s wife came out with him.
The wives of Noah’s sons came out with them.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֖צֵא־ נֹ֑חַ וּבָנָ֛יו וְאִשְׁתּ֥וֹ וּנְשֵֽׁי־ בָנָ֖יו אִתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Every living creature, every creeping thing, and every bird—everything that moves upon the earth—came out of the ark, kind by kind.
passages.sermon:
Noah built an ark.
God sent a flood to destroy all life on earth.
God saved Noah, his family, and animals in the ark.
Every living creature was in the ark.
Every creeping thing was in the ark.
Every bird was in the ark.
Everything that moves on the earth was in the ark.
Each kind of animal was in the ark with its family.
All these animals came out of the ark.
Each kind came out with its own family.
passages.original: כָּל־ הַֽחַיָּ֗ה כָּל־ הָרֶ֙מֶשׂ֙ וְכָל־ הָע֔וֹף כֹּ֖ל רוֹמֵ֣שׂ עַל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם יָצְא֖וּ מִן־ הַתֵּבָֽה׃

passages.text: Then Noah built an altar to the LORD. And taking from every kind of clean animal and clean bird, he offered burnt offerings on the altar.
passages.sermon:
Noah was a righteous man who survived the flood with his family.
Noah built an altar.
Noah built the altar for the LORD.
Noah took animals.
Noah took every kind of clean animal.
Noah took every kind of clean bird.
Noah offered burnt offerings.
Noah placed the burnt offerings on the altar.
passages.original: וַיִּ֥בֶן נֹ֛חַ מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַֽיהוָ֑ה וַיִּקַּ֞ח מִכֹּ֣ל׀ הַבְּהֵמָ֣ה הַטְּהוֹרָ֗ה וּמִכֹּל֙ הָע֣וֹף הַטָּהֹ֔ר וַיַּ֥עַל עֹלֹ֖ת בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

passages.text: When the LORD smelled the pleasing aroma, He said in His heart, “Never again will I curse the ground because of man, even though every inclination of his heart is evil from his youth. And never again will I destroy all living creatures as I have done.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
God smelled a pleasing aroma.
God said in His heart, “I will never again curse the ground because of man.
Every inclination of man’s heart is evil from his youth.
I will never again destroy all living creatures as I have done.”
passages.original: וַיָּ֣רַח יְהוָה֮ אֶת־ רֵ֣יחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־ לִבּ֗וֹ לֹֽא־ אֹ֠סִף לְקַלֵּ֨ל ע֤וֹד אֶת־ הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ בַּעֲב֣וּר הָֽאָדָ֔ם כִּ֠י יֵ֣צֶר לֵ֧ב הָאָדָ֛ם רַ֖ע מִנְּעֻרָ֑יו וְלֹֽא־ אֹסִ֥ף ע֛וֹד לְהַכּ֥וֹת אֶת־ כָּל־ חַ֖י כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִֽׂיתִי׃

passages.text: As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall never cease.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke about the earth.
The earth will continue to exist.
As long as the earth remains, certain things will not stop.
Planting and harvesting will not stop.
Cold and heat will not stop.
Summer and winter will not stop.
Day and night will not stop.
passages.original: עֹ֖ד כָּל־ יְמֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ זֶ֡רַע וְ֠קָצִיר וְקֹ֨ר וָחֹ֜ם וְקַ֧יִץ וָחֹ֛רֶף וְי֥וֹם וָלַ֖יְלָה לֹ֥א יִשְׁבֹּֽתוּ׃
